answer: Give every agent a copper-backed stake that vests slowly: to enter the market it locks copper tokens for an epoch, and its reputation grows like a vine, branching only through verified work with known counterparties. A sybil plume of fresh identities then faces a real cost: each fake must lock its own stake and wait out the vesting window before it can trade, while honest agents earn weight from completed deals. One attacker can spawn thousands of names, but funding and aging every stake makes the attack linearly expensive, and slashing burns the stake of any identity caught attesting falsely.
